title: 2053-alphaprobe-dag-retrieval-biased-evolution
universal_lens: Alpha mining is formalized as a stochastic process over a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Nodes represent factor expressions, while edges denote evolutionary transitions. A Bayesian retriever navigates this topological space, optimizing an objective function that balances exploitation of high-quality nodes with exploration of novel subgraphs, fundamentally unifying isolated generation and iterative evolution.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the DAG represents the latent space of predictive sports signals. The Bayesian retriever acts as a conformal inference engine, selecting seed features based on posterior probabilities derived from historical ICIR. Topology penalties enforce anti-collinearity, ensuring diverse feature extraction across varying game states and environmental conditions.
gse_mapping: For GSE, situational reasoning maps to ancestral trace conditioning. Instead of local parent-child edits, the generator consumes the full lineage of a tactical primitive within the DAG. This allows state-transitions to be context-aware, preventing redundant search in the tactical playbook and adapting dynamically to evolving in-game regimes.

reasoning_traces.think:
The AlphaPROBE framework mathematically elevates automated factor mining from a flat, decoupled search space to a structured, navigable Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Traditional paradigms—Decoupled Factor Generation and Iterative Factor Evolution—suffer from a lack of global structural awareness, leading to redundant search trajectories and limited diversity in the resulting signal zoo. By defining factors as nodes and their evolutionary refinements as directed edges, the system introduces a topological constraint that inherently penalizes redundant exploration.

The core operator is the Bayesian Factor Retriever, which formulates seed selection as a probabilistic inference problem. It computes a posterior probability that harmonizes exploitation (driven by empirical metrics like absolute ICIR) with exploration (guided by priors and a topology penalty). Crucially, the inclusion of a Natural-Language Feedback (NLF) term allows the retriever to incorporate semantic distinctiveness, preventing the algorithm from converging prematurely on numerically similar but structurally identical factors.

Once a seed is retrieved, the DAG-aware Factor Generator executes the transition. Unlike local parent-child mutations, this generator conditions its output on the full ancestral trace of the selected node. This deep contextual conditioning ensures that new factors are non-redundant refinements tailored to the specific evolutionary path taken. The retention of evicted factors within the graph $G$ preserves topological completeness, allowing the system to remember failed evolutionary branches and avoid re-traversing them. This dual mechanism of principled retrieval and trace-conditioned generation constitutes a rigorous mathematical unification of global view and local refinement.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This methodology inherits from Genetic Programming (GP) and Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), but diverges by explicitly modeling the global dependency graph rather than relying on isolated fitness landscapes. It echoes the historical shift from Markovian local optimizations to persistent memory architectures in reinforcement learning, specifically addressing the 'catastrophic forgetting' of successful but discarded topological structures in prior automated alpha discovery systems like AlphaGen.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-theoretic perspective, the AlphaPROBE agent models the market (or sporting environment) as an adversarial entity constantly shifting regime boundaries. The Bayesian retriever acts as a cognitive controller, anticipating that previously dominant factors will decay. By balancing exploitation with topological exploration, the agent simulates an opposing force that punishes overfitting to narrow structural niches, thereby enforcing robustness against unseen regime shifts and maintaining a diverse arsenal of predictive primitives.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the topological penalty fails to adequately suppress highly collinear subgraphs. If the DAG degenerates into dense clusters of semantically identical factors, the ancestral trace conditioning loses its discriminative power, reverting the system to a noisy, flat-pool baseline. Furthermore, if the LLM generator cannot effectively parse long ancestral traces, the contextual advantage vanishes, triggering a rejection gate based on compute inefficiency and lack of test-season RankIC stability.
